transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, I guess I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my face. The left side of it, specifically. It looks really crooked and... just messed up. 

It's basically all I think about. Like, when I'm at work at the warehouse, or if I try to go to salsa night, I feel like everyone is staring at it and noticing how bad it is. People tell me they don't see anything when I ask them, but I just can't stop focusing on it. It's really taking a toll on me.
Do you ever feel completely certain that the left side of your face is deformed, even when other people tell you they don't see anything wrong?

Yeah, I do. I mean... I hear them when they say they don't see it, but I just figure they're being nice, or maybe they just aren't looking closely enough. Because when I look in the mirror, it's... it's just obvious to me. It's right there. So, yeah, I'm completely sure it's messed up, no matter what anyone else tells me.
Has anyone else ever told you that the left side of your face actually looks deformed?

No, nobody has ever actually said that to me. Like I said, whenever I ask people about it, they always say they don't see anything wrong. But... I don't know, I just don't believe them. It feels like they're just trying to spare my feelings or something.
Do you spend a lot of time checking the left side of your face in mirrors or other reflective surfaces?

Yeah, I do. A lot, actually. Um, especially at work. Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I always stop in the bathroom and just... stare in the mirror. I keep checking that side of my face, adjusting my cap to try and cover it up, and just rubbing at the same spot over and over. Sometimes I get stuck in there doing it for so long that I end up late getting back. My picking numbers fall behind, and my boss has been getting on my case about it. It's just hard to stop once I start looking.
Do you believe with complete certainty that the left side of your face is actually deformed?
Yeah, I really do. I know you asked that a minute ago, but... yeah, I'm completely sure. I look at it, and it's just deformed. There's no doubt in my mind about it, no matter what anybody else says.
Do you think the amount of time you spend worrying about your face is excessive?

Um... I'm not really sure if I'd call it excessive. I mean, I know it takes up a lot of time, and like I said, it messes with my picking numbers at work. But... since it's a real deformity, it just feels like something I have to pay attention to, you know? I don't know, I guess I just haven't really thought about it like that. It's just what I have to do.
Aside from your face, do you have any other beliefs that other people would say aren’t true?

No, I don't think so. Um... it's really just my face that's the problem. I don't have any other beliefs like that, or anything else that people would say isn't true. Everything else is just... normal, I guess.
Do you do things over and over because of how your face looks, like checking mirrors, covering it, or touching that area?

Yeah, I do. Um... especially at work. Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I always go to the bathroom and just keep checking my face in the mirror. I'll stand there fixing my cap and just rubbing at that same spot on my face over and over. 

I do it a lot. Sometimes I take so long doing it that I'm late getting back to work, and my picking numbers fall behind. Then my boss gets on me about it again. But I just can't stop checking it.
When you feel like people are staring at your face, do you think they really are noticing it?

Yeah, I do. I mean, it's so obvious, how could they not notice it? When I'm out on the floor and people look my way, I know they're seeing it. It's not just in my head—it's right there on my face. So yeah, I definitely think they're staring at it.
If your face looked completely normal to you, would you still feel anxious that other people were judging you in social situations?

I don't think so. I mean, if my face wasn't... like this, I wouldn't have any reason to worry. I don't really care what people think about me otherwise, it's just... I know they're looking at my face. So if it was normal, I think I'd be fine around people.
Is there any part of you that thinks you might be mistaken about your face being deformed?

No, not at all. I mean... I look at it every single day. I see exactly what it looks like. It's not like I'm just imagining things, it's right there in the mirror. So, no, I don't think I'm mistaken about it.
Have you ever tried to resist or stop checking your face in the mirror?

I've tried, but... I just can't stop. Like, before I go back out on the inventory floor, I always end up in the bathroom. I just have to check the mirror. I'll stand there fixing my cap, trying to get it to cover my face right, and... I just end up rubbing at the same spot over and over. Sometimes I'm in there so long that I end up being late getting back. My picking numbers fall behind, and then my boss gets on me about it again. But I just can't seem to stop myself from checking.
